Flash Q1 -
This "Invisible Giant" of the Indian retail landscape operates the most efficient logistics network in the country, despite not being a household name in the traditional commercial sense. Long before the "Big Box" retail explosion of the 2000s, this entity perfected a high-volume, low-margin blueprint that modern giants like DMart and Reliance Retail have since adopted as their North Star.
To solve the logistical nightmare of serving over 12 million authorized beneficiaries across every corner of the subcontinent, this organization bypassed the traditional "Distributor-Wholesaler-Retailer" chain. Instead, they pioneered a Centralized Procurement and Regional Depot System. By acting as a "Single Buyer" for the entire nation, they negotiate massive discounts directly from manufacturers. These goods are then moved from factory gates to 34 regional hubs, and finally to over 3,900 point-of-sale units, virtually eliminating the cost of middlemen.
In many consumer-goods boardrooms, this entity is considered the ultimate "litmus test" for a product's success; if it isn't listed here, it hasn't truly arrived in the Indian market.
For 10 points, identify this massive, institutionalized retail network—the largest of its kind in India—whose "direct-from-manufacturer" logistics model paved the way for the country's modern supermarket revolution.

Q2 . In the annals of Indian industry, while the 1990s were marked by the liberalization of the economy, the early 2000s saw the "Industrial Revolution of Emotion." One Mumbai-based manufacturing hub abandoned the "artistic" approach to content creation in favor of a Fordist assembly line. Operating on grueling 24/7 triple-shifts, this facility functioned as a high-volume factory where "creative units" were standardized, processed, and shipped with mechanical precision.
The "factory floor" was governed by a strict K-branded blueprint, ensuring that every product—regardless of the specific cast—adhered to a rigorous set of specifications: high-contrast lighting, repetitive acoustic cues, and a "modular" narrative structure that allowed for the seamless replacement of "faulty parts" without halting the production line. This industrial scale was so massive that it effectively dictated the prime-time consumption habits of an entire subcontinent, treating domestic drama as a commodity to be mass-produced. Identify the company and the founder.
